description: Gripper Gen 15: full printable handheld gripper built around the Gen 14 fingers. Jake (voice): 'I'm happy with Gen 14. Let's move forward with making it printable. Gen 15: keep that, but from the photos add the rest of it: the actual attachment mechanism and stuff, and the ability to attach a camera.' Spec: keep the Gen 14 finger shape (voice-fe67959c) as-is, only adjusting it for printability (wall thickness, tip strength, hole sizes, print orientation, tolerances at the pivots). From all the reference photos in cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_*.png, add the rest of the device: the pivot/linkage plate and finger carrier blocks, the hand-mount frame, and an Insta360 X4/X5-size camera mount on the back of the hand with the lens facing forward. Earlier asks from Jake still apply: mounting and mechanism sit ABOVE the hand, keep the thumb-index web as empty as possible; three straps (wrist, index finger, thumb) modeled as separate non-printed parts, with slots that also fit zip ties. Output printable STLs per part plus a parts list, and show the assembly in the gallery with the open/close slider and exploded view. New version only.

results.detailed_description:
Gen 15 is already built to the original spec, so I left it alone. That covers the Gen 14 fingers tuned for printing, the thumb and index carriers, the pivot plate, the hand frame with wrist-strap slots, and the Insta360 X4/X5 mount. The three straps are drawn as non-printed parts, the slots take zip ties, and there's a BOM and seven print STLs.

I re-ran the check results and they all pass: swing, web clearance, geometry, export and mesh. It's in the gallery as "Gen 15" with the open/close slider and exploded view.

The simplified version (side pads, no wrist, no drawn straps) is filed separately as Gen 16 (voice-258bb62c) and is in the agent queue. Close this one if Gen 15 looks right in the gallery.

results.notes: Jake (voice): 'Maybe we need all those things to go for Gen 16?' SUPERSEDED: ignore the last two notes (no straps drawn; radical simplification without the wrist attachment). Those go into a separate Gen 16. Finish Gen 15 as originally specified in the description. .

results.identified_issue: Architecture read from photos: each finger is moved by its own digit, with no sync linkage. The carrier holds the pivot nut (side-entry M4 nyloc) because Gen 14's pivot origin sits at the finger's thin root lip (only ~2 mm of wall), so a bore there would break out. The finger bolts to the carrier through honeycomb holes (-11.2,16.3) and (-11.2,27.4) in the finger frame, opened to 3.2 mm. Hole count stays 33. The orientation is a right hand, palm down: viewed from +Y, +X is on the viewer's left, so the thumb is on the +X/'Right' finger. The hand dimensions and the back-of-hand height are nominal guesses. The slot clip uses offset(-ridge_wall-0.05), because exactly -ridge_wall made the grooves' stop line land on the edge and broke the mesh. Under the manifold backend, intersection() with a bare for() treats each child separately, so it is wrapped in union(). Scripts/publish_designs.py (untracked, local only) got a v015 → 'Gen 15' entry that is not committed. VERSIONS.txt is untracked too, so its new line is also uncommitted. STLs are gitignored.
results.summary: Gen 15 is in the gallery: the Gen 14 fingers plus everything from the photos to wear it and print it. That's thumb and index carriers, a pivot plate, a hand frame, an Insta360 X4/X5 camera mount, and three straps, with STLs and a parts list.
results.user_reply_draft: Hey Jake, Gen 15 is up in the gallery. It's the Gen 14 fingers you liked plus the rest of the device: thumb and index carriers with straps, a pivot plate, a hand frame on the back of your hand, and a mount for an Insta360 X4/X5 facing forward. The fingers' shape is unchanged, just tuned to print cleanly. There's a parts list with every screw and strap. The hand sizing is a first guess, so expect to adjust the strap positions after a test fit.

results.notes: Jake (voice): 'Focus on significant simplicity. Make it much simpler. It doesn't need that whole arm attachment bit; if it doesn't attach to my wrist, that's okay. It just needs a flat piece on the side that I can put my fingers in, my thumb on the other side, and a strap that goes over. Really simple.' Revised scope: drop the wrist/forearm attachment entirely. Each finger gets a simple flat pad/plate on its side: fingers on one, thumb on the other, each with one slot for a strap or zip tie over the top. Keep the Gen 14 fingers, the pivot and the camera mount, but minimize part count and complexity everywhere else. .
Jake (voice): 'We don't need to actually draw the straps on there. That's unnecessary.' Don't model or render the straps at all. Just keep the strap/zip-tie slots in the printed parts. .

summary: Gen 15 needs a full printable handheld gripper: the unchanged Gen 14 fingers plus pivot plate, carrier blocks, above-hand mount frame, and forward-facing Insta360 camera mount. Deliver per-part STLs, a parts list, and a gallery assembly with open/close slider and exploded view, with three separately modeled straps and strap/zip-tie slots.
